Chapter 10: The Ongoing Journey of Self-Reliance
You know, there’s really no finish line when it comes to self-reliance. There’s no moment when you can say, "Okay, I’ve made it. I’m done." Life just doesn’t work that way. Instead, it keeps tossing new challenges our way—each one asking us to dig a little deeper, find new reserves of courage, honesty, or adaptability.
The journey is never straight. Sure, you’ll have setbacks and stumbles. You’ll doubt yourself at times, but you’ll also surprise yourself with those sudden flashes of insight that come out of nowhere.
Think about a parent who’s always felt sure of their approach, only to find themselves thrown off by a teenager’s rebellion. Suddenly, what used to work just doesn’t anymore, and the way forward feels completely uncertain. In the thick of that frustration, they remember—sometimes you just need to listen. Listen to your own gut, and really hear what your child is saying. It’s messy, definitely. But with time, trust can grow again, and a new kind of relationship starts to take shape.
A lot of people imagine self-reliance as a solo act—standing strong, alone, against the world. But honestly, it’s not that simple. Sure, you need to think for yourself and act on your own convictions, but real self-reliance also means staying connected. It’s about learning from others, owning up to your mistakes, and not being afraid to ask for help. Sometimes, the strongest people are the ones who know how to balance independence with a healthy dose of humility.
It’s tempting to look for certainty—to chase after some kind of formula that guarantees success. But if you’ve lived long enough, you know life just doesn’t play by those rules. Every new stage brings its own questions, its own demands. The real challenge? Staying open, keeping your mind curious, and trusting that, even when things don’t make sense, the process itself is worth it.
Picture a writer, totally stuck with creative block. She tries every trick she knows, but nothing seems to work. Finally, she lets go—drops her expectations—and just writes whatever feels true in that moment. Suddenly, the words start flowing, and the joy comes rushing back. The lesson here isn’t about mastering a craft or finding the perfect trick. It’s about trust: trusting the process, trusting yourself, and believing that each small step matters.
So, what becomes clear is this: self-reliance isn’t about arriving at some final destination. It’s about embracing the journey, showing up day after day, with honesty and courage—always willing to start again, no matter what happened yesterday.
